transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because my body just feels kind of out of my control. At first I was pacing around my apartment all night, writing these supper-club notes and not really stopping. And now it’s like the opposite—everything is slowed down. My sister says it takes me forever just to get my shoes on.
Have you been feeling unusually happy or excited recently?

Yeah. After I got fired, I felt weirdly… unstoppable, like excited in a way that didn’t really make sense. But it also came with this edge—if anyone questioned what I was doing or told me to slow down, I’d snap at them, like they were trying to ruin everything for me.
How long have you been feeling slowed down like this?
It’s been about three months now. The heavy, slowed-down feeling has pretty much been there that whole time.
Have you been feeling sad or empty most of the time since you started feeling slowed down?
I don’t really know how to answer that. I feel heavy and kind of shut down, but I’m not sure I’d call it sad or empty most of the time. It’s more like… slowed and stuck.
Have you experienced any strange thoughts or heard voices that others couldn't hear since you've been feeling slowed down?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t heard voices or had anything like that. My thoughts feel… off sometimes, but not strange like that.
Have you had a period of at least two weeks where you felt sad or empty most of the time since you started feeling slowed down?
I’m not sure. I don’t think I’ve had a clear two-week stretch where I’d say I was sad or empty most of the time. It’s more just been this slowed-down, stuck feeling.
Did you have a period where you felt unstoppable and excited before you started feeling slowed down?

Yeah. After I got fired, I had this stretch where I felt kind of unstoppable, like I was really excited and sure I could do anything. But if someone questioned what I was doing or told me to slow down, I’d get really angry, like they were trying to mess everything up for me.
How long did this unstoppable and excited feeling last after you got fired?
About four months, I think. It started after I got fired from the restaurant and kind of kept going from there.
Did your unstoppable and excited feeling after getting fired cause problems in your relationships or daily life?

Yeah, it caused a lot of problems. I couldn’t really keep work plans straight, or figure out rent stuff, or follow through on things I told my family I’d do. It got to the point where my sister had to take me to a crisis clinic because I just wasn’t able to get basic responsibilities organized on my own.
Did your feeling of being unstoppable and excited last less than 4 months after you got fired?
No, I wouldn’t say less than that. It was about four months, starting after I got fired from the restaurant.
Have you lost interest in activities you normally enjoy since you started feeling slowed down?

Yeah. A lot of the things I usually like just feel kind of empty now. Cooking, taking food photos, listening to music, playing pickup soccer, even volunteering—stuff that normally keeps me steady—it all feels flat. I know I used to care about it, but I can’t really feel that right now.
Have you had any periods where you felt sad or empty most of the time since you started feeling slowed down?
I’m not really sure how to answer that. I’ve felt slowed down and kind of flat, but I don’t know if I’d call it sad or empty most of the time. It’s more like… I don’t feel much.
Has your slowed-down feeling lasted for at least two weeks without any significant improvement?
Yeah, definitely more than two weeks. It’s been about three months now where I’ve felt heavy and slowed down, without it really letting up.
Has there been any point since you started feeling slowed down where you felt sad or empty nearly every day for at least two weeks?
I don’t know. I can’t really say there was a clear two-week stretch where I felt sad or empty every day. It’s been more like feeling flat and slowed down, kind of numb.
Has there been a two-week period since you started feeling slowed down where you felt either sad, empty, or both nearly every day?
I’m not sure I can say that. I’ve been feeling slowed down and kind of numb, but I don’t remember a clear two-week stretch where I felt sad or empty nearly every day.
Has your slowed-down feeling lasted for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks at any point since it started?
Yeah. Most of the day, pretty much every day lately. I feel like my body just won’t move right—like it takes me forever to do basic stuff, even getting my shoes on. My sister’s noticed it too.
Has there been a two-week period where your slowed-down feeling was present most of the day, nearly every day?

Yes, for at least the last couple weeks it’s been like that most of the day, nearly every day. I’m moving so slowly it feels like my body isn’t really listening to me. My sister even says it takes me forever just to get my shoes on.
Have you had any significant weight loss or gain since you started feeling slowed down?
Yeah, I think I’ve lost some weight. I’m not trying to, but my jeans are looser lately. Some days I barely eat—like just coffee or maybe a tortilla—because food just tastes like cardboard.
Has your slowed-down feeling lasted for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks without any significant improvement?

Yeah, it hasn’t really let up. Most of the day I feel like my body just won’t move right. At first I was kind of the opposite—pacing around all night making these supper-club notes—but lately I’m so slowed down my sister says it takes me forever just to put my shoes on.
Do you think your slowed-down feeling is related to feeling sad or unhappy?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I don’t feel good about it, but I can’t tell if the slowness is because I’m sad or if being this slowed down is what’s making me feel worse. It’s kind of all mixed together.
